name: Leah Buzek
title: Program strategist and systems designer
statement: This is a working notebook rather than a finished catalogue — a record of designing survivor-centered systems, researching the trauma that caregiving creates, and building the infrastructure nonprofit programs run on. The pieces here sit across program strategy, research, policy, academic work, and the talks that carry it into the field.
bio: I'm a program strategist and systems designer who translates ambiguous, high-stakes problems into usable infrastructure — trauma-informed onboarding, participatory governance, statewide training pipelines, the connective tissue that lets survivor-centered programs actually run. I founded IncuBrighter, a civic R&D incubator that channels the expertise of people with lived experience of poverty, trauma, and systemic inequity into program design, training, and policy advocacy.

Since 2023 I've been building the TRACEs framework (Trauma & Relational Adversity in Caregiving Environments), a six-domain assessment tool for identifying relational strain, burnout, and trauma load in multi-system-involved families, drawn from care ethics, cognitive load theory, and vulnerability analysis. It's the throughline behind most of the research and talks here.

As an AmeriCorps VISTA I direct statewide survivor-engagement work in Ohio — launching the Survivor Voices Council and a statewide needs assessment on domestic violence and substance use among them — after two years as a Family Peer Supporter co-managing statewide behavioral health programs. I graduated from Ohio University with a B.S. in Integrated Studies in May 2026 and started my Master of Public Service at the University of Arkansas's Clinton School two weeks later.
availability: Open to program strategy, research, and speaking collaborations.
